title: Transport of evaluation biduality across an invertible dualizing twist
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $g:T\to V$ be a scheme morphism, and use ordinary constant-$A$ modules on small etale sites and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Use derived tensor and internal Hom [def-kun-derived-tensor, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Assume the inverse image $g^*$ is exact and strong symmetric monoidal. Let $\Omega\in D(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $\Omega'\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, and fix an isomorphism $\theta:g^*\Omega\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega'\otimes_A^L J$, where $J=Q[m]$, $m\in\mathbf Z$, and $Q$ is an etale locally constant rank-one $A_T$-module sheaf with a tensor inverse. Put $D=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\Omega)$ and $D'=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\Omega')$. For any object $B$, define $\delta_B:B\to DDB$ as the transpose of evaluation with its tensor factors interchanged by the symmetry; use the same convention for $\delta'$.

Let $K\in D(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and suppose the tensor-adjoint internal-Hom comparisons
$$\beta_{B,\Omega}:g^*R\mathcal Hom_A(B,\Omega)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(g^*B,g^*\Omega)\qquad(B=K,DK)$$
are isomorphisms and respect evaluation: $\mathrm{ev}\circ(\beta_{B,\Omega}\otimes 1)=g^*\mathrm{ev}_{B,\Omega}$ under the monoidal comparison. Write $P=g^*K$. The canonical invertible-factor Hom isomorphisms give
$$\alpha:g^*DK\xrightarrow{\sim}D'P\otimes_A^L J.$$
Let $\gamma:g^*DDK\xrightarrow{\sim}D'D'P$ be the composite of $\beta_{DK,\Omega}$, the substitution of $\alpha$ in the first Hom variable and $\theta$ in the second, and cancellation
$$R\mathcal Hom_A(D'P\otimes_A^L J,\Omega'\otimes_A^L J)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(D'P,\Omega').$$
Then $\gamma\circ g^*\delta_K=\delta'_P$. No biduality isomorphism or constructibility is assumed.

proof.text: First check that the shifted line really is invertible for derived tensor. Choose the sheaf inverse $Q^{-1}$ of $Q$. On an etale cover trivializing $Q$, the isomorphism $Q\otimes Q^{-1}\cong A_T$ trivializes $Q^{-1}$ too. Thus tensor with either sheaf is exact, checked on this cover where it is the identity; both are flat. Their one-term shifted complexes are K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure]. The total-complex definition [def-kun-derived-tensor] now computes $Q[m]\otimes_A^LQ^{-1}[-m]$ and its reverse as their degree-zero sheaf products, with zero differential. The given sheaf inverse isomorphisms give both products $A_T$. Hence $I=Q^{-1}[-m]$ is a two-sided inverse of $J$. In the remaining steps suppress monoidal associators, put $F=g^*$, $W=\Omega'$, $P=FK$ and $H=[P,W]=D'P$, and write $[X,Y]=R\mathcal Hom_A(X,Y)$, $e_{X,Y}:[X,Y]\otimes X\to Y$.

source.place: Shifted line invertibility; bounded-flat K-flatness is sites-cohomology-lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat (Tag 06YQ); total tensor as in def-kun-derived-tensor.

proof.text: By [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] on $(T_{\mathrm{et}},A_T)$ and $(V_{\mathrm{et}},A_V)$, derived tensor, its Koszul symmetry and $R\mathcal Hom_A$ make these derived categories closed symmetric monoidal with evaluation $e$ as counit, which are the hypotheses of [lem-sf-invertible-factor-hom-cancellation]; with $I$ from step 1 it applies to $J$. Use its $t$. The composite $b=[P,\theta]\circ\beta_{K,\Omega}:FDK\xrightarrow{\sim}[P,W\otimes J]$ is an isomorphism by the hypotheses. Define $\alpha=t_{P,W,J}^{-1}\circ b:FDK\xrightarrow{\sim}H\otimes J$. This is precisely the canonical twisted dual comparison in the statement. No dualizability of $P$ is needed: the helper allows arbitrary $X=P$ and $Y=W$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, returned step 7: construction of the specified twisted dual comparison.

proof.text: For the second comparison set $u=[\alpha^{-1},\theta]\circ\beta_{DK,\Omega}:FDDK\xrightarrow{\sim}[H\otimes J,W\otimes J]$. Here the first Hom variable is contravariant, so the substitution uses $\alpha^{-1}$. By [lem-sf-invertible-factor-hom-cancellation], $s_{H,W,J}$ is an isomorphism. Define $\gamma=s_{H,W,J}^{-1}\circ u:FDDK\xrightarrow{\sim}[H,W]$. This is exactly the prescribed composite of the second beta comparison, substitution, and cancellation.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, returned step 7: second comparison and cancellation in both Hom variables.

proof.text:
Record the evaluation equations that will determine the arrow, rather than merely the objects. The evaluation-preserving beta hypotheses and the two displayed equations of [lem-sf-invertible-factor-hom-cancellation] give
$$\theta\circ F(e_{K,\Omega})=(e_{P,W}\otimes1_J)\circ(1_H\otimes\sigma_{J,P})\circ(\alpha\otimes1_P),$$
$$\theta\circ F(e_{DK,\Omega})=(e_{H,W}\otimes1_J)\circ(\gamma\otimes\alpha).$$
The domains are respectively $FDK\otimes P$ and $FDDK\otimes FDK$. The first equation substitutes $t\alpha=b$ into the first normalization; the second substitutes $s\gamma=u$ into the second normalization. Naturality of the adjunction of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] in all three variables (so $e_{X,Y}\circ(1\otimes\varphi)=e_{X',Y}\circ([\varphi,Y]\otimes1)$ for $\varphi:X'\to X$, and $\theta\circ e=e\circ([X,\theta]\otimes1)$) handles the changes of variables. These are equations between the actual evaluation maps, using only the assumed strong monoidal comparisons of $F$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, returned step 7: evaluation equations for alpha and gamma.

proof.text:
Put $f=\gamma\circ F\delta_K:P\to[H,W]$. By the defining transpose equation for $\delta_K$,
$$e_{DK,\Omega}\circ(\delta_K\otimes1_{DK})=e_{K,\Omega}\circ\sigma_{K,DK}.$$
Apply the strong symmetric monoidal functor $F$, postcompose with $\theta$, and precompose with $1_P\otimes\alpha^{-1}$. Substitute the two equations of step 4. On $P\otimes H\otimes J$ this gives
$$\bigl(e_{H,W}\circ(f\otimes1_H)\bigr)\otimes1_J=(e_{P,W}\otimes1_J)\circ(1_H\otimes\sigma_{J,P})\circ\sigma_{P,H\otimes J}.$$
Indeed naturality moves $\alpha$ across the pulled-back symmetry. The hexagon writes $\sigma_{P,H\otimes J}=(1_H\otimes\sigma_{P,J})\circ(\sigma_{P,H}\otimes1_J)$. Since $\sigma_{J,P}\sigma_{P,J}=1$, the right side is $(e_{P,W}\circ\sigma_{P,H})\otimes1_J$. This calculation uses the naturality, involutivity and hexagon of the symmetry from [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal], including the Koszul signs when $J$ is an odd shift.

source.place: Proof paragraph 4, returned step 7: direct tensor-adjunction computation of the double-dual arrow.

proof.text:
Tensor the last equality with $I$ from step 1 and compose with $J\otimes I\cong\mathbf1$ and the unitors. Naturality and the tensor bifunctor laws remove the common factor $J$, giving
$$e_{H,W}\circ(f\otimes1_H)=e_{P,W}\circ\sigma_{P,H}.$$
By definition the right side is the uncurrying of $\delta'_P:P\to[H,W]$. The left side is the uncurrying of $f$. The inverse-adjunction and evaluation formulas in [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws], using symmetry to interchange its left-evaluation convention with our right-evaluation convention, identify these with the corresponding adjunction images. Since that adjunction map, the bijection of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] whose inverse is $u\mapsto e_{H,W}\circ(u\otimes1_H)$, is injective, $f=\delta'_P$, which is the required $\gamma\circ g^*\delta_K=\delta'_P$.

lean.note: Ordinary constant-A module-valued etale sheaves, using the existing derivedTensor, derivedHom, derivedTensorHomAdjunction, canonical pullback tensor comparison and packaged Koszul symmetry. Only the target associator is exposed as a witness, identified by HEq with the actual descended associator, to avoid costly conversion between definitionally equal tensor presentations. The two generic proposition definitions spell out beta evaluation normalization and the three conclusion equations. Alpha and gamma are uniquely specified by uncurrying the canonical t and s normalizations; the final equality concerns the actual evaluation-defined bidual arrows. No extra constructibility, boundedness, dualizability or bidual-isomorphism hypothesis.
